note: License policy for the modules linked into ./cmd/lit. Every allowed_licenses entry is a permissive license with no copyleft obligation that conflicts with lit's MIT 'free for any purpose' guarantee. A linked module whose classified license (per tools/licenses' classifier, the same one that builds LICENSE-REPORT.md) is not in allowed_licenses must appear in module_exceptions with a reason, or the CI license-policy gate (`go run ./tools/licenses -check`, and TestDependencyLicensesArePermitted) fails. This is the single committed policy file; edit it to accept a new license class (allowed_licenses) or to record a per-module, human-verified exception (module_exceptions). See links-supply-chain-w6m9.3.

module_exceptions.reason: fslock's LICENSE is LGPLv3 WITH a static-linking exception (it grants the right to link the library statically without the resulting binary inheriting LGPL obligations). The classifier matches the LGPL text and reports LGPL-3.0; the exception clause makes it permissive for lit's static linking. Human-verified against the module's LICENSE.

buzhash ships a non-standard, profanely-worded WTFPL variant that the classifier cannot match above its confidence threshold, so it reports Unknown. WTFPL is a permissive public-domain-equivalent license. Human-verified against the module's LICENSE; the 'Unknown' here is a classifier limitation, not an unvetted license.
